Write a model as JSON, and read it back

Source: R/json.R
pmx_write_json.Rd

pmx_write_json() writes the representation as a JSON document and pmx_read_json() reads one back. The document holds the model's seven components as data, so a model read from JSON is the model that was written: the same parameters, statements, provenance and all. It is zupmxio's own representation, not a file standard (design D3).

Usage

pmx_write_json(model, file = NULL, pretty = TRUE)

pmx_read_json(file)

Arguments

model

A model read by one of the pmx_read_*() functions.

file

For pmx_write_json(), the path to write, or NULL to only return the text. For pmx_read_json(), the path of a JSON file.

pretty

Whether to indent the JSON.

Value

pmx_write_json(): the JSON text, invisibly when file is given. pmx_read_json(): a model. A file that is not a zupmxio JSON model is a zupmxio_parse_error.

Details

Statements and expressions are R code in strings ("cl <- tcl * exp(eta.cl)"), constants are numbers. JSON has no infinity, so Inf and -Inf are the strings "Inf" and "-Inf"; a missing value is null. Numbers are written in the fewest digits that read back exactly.

Both functions need the zujson package, and raise an error of class zupmxio_engine_error without it.

See also

Other readers: pmx_read_mrgsolve(), pmx_read_nonmem(), pmx_read_rxode2(), pmx_read_tables()

Examples

path <- system.file(
  "corpus", "onecmt-oral", "model.ctl",
  package = "zupmxio"
)
model <- pmx_read_nonmem(path)
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
pmx_write_json(model, file)
identical(pmx_read_json(file), model)
#> [1] TRUE
